description: Tech enthusiast passionate about AI, innovation, and solving real-world problems with NASA data. Looking to build an impactful and creative solution with a strong team. Seeking teammates interested in AI/ML, coding, UI/UX, data visualization, research, astronomy/Earth science, or storytelling. Open to anyone who is motivated, collaborative, and ready to contribute!
summary: CombustionLens is a source-linked research workspace that helps researchers explore NASA microgravity combustion findings and see where they do and don't apply to future missions. Its evidence explorer links four NASA campaign summaries (BASS, FLEX, Saffire VI, SoFIE-GEL) to their original sources, ranks them with a disclosed, explainable method, and keeps published observations separate from our interpretations. A mission-applicability check compares gravity, fuel class, oxygen, pressure, ventilation and geometry for orbital, lunar and Mars-transit contexts, marking each as aligned, mismatched or unknown, so missing evidence is visible and unknown conditions are never treated as safe. Users can export source-linked research briefs. A research backend retrieves and reranks passages from NASA Technical Reports Server reports with page-level citations and numerical checks. It is a research prototype, not a flight-qualified fire-safety tool, and it does not predict fire risk.
details:
The Problem
NASA has decades of microgravity combustion results, but a correct finding can still be wrong for a given spacecraft. Gravity, fuel geometry, atmosphere and ventilation can all make a result non-transferable. Finding a result is not enough. Researchers need to know whether it applies to their mission.

What It Does

  • Evidence Explorer: four curated NASA campaign summaries with searchable findings, explainable ranking by mission priority (for example detection and extinction), and three mission contexts. It runs without a backend or API key.
  • Mission Applicability: six physical boundary checks that give aligned, mismatch or unknown results, plus exportable research questions. For lunar surface contexts it shows an explicit partial-gravity evidence gap instead of inventing a threshold.
  • Research Backend: dense retrieval over NASA reports, cross-encoder reranking, page-level citations and numerical-claim checks. Without a generative model it returns labeled source excerpts.
  • Verified Comparator: only independently verified experiment records are eligible. None are verified yet, so the comparator shows an empty state on purpose.
  • Exports: Markdown research briefs that carry citations, limitations and mission context.

Data and Evidence
We collected 6 NASA Technical Reports Server reports (549 pages) and kept their rights determinations and SHA-256 hashes. Three reports with explicit public-use permission are indexed as 457 passages. We also staged 31 BASS test-condition rows and 8 Saffire measurements, which await independent review.

Tools and Technology
React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS and Recharts on the frontend. Python, FastAPI, ChromaDB, sentence-transformers, DuckDB and PyMuPDF on the backend.

Validation
68 backend tests and 20 frontend tests passed, and the production build succeeded. A small retrieval benchmark scored 8/8 development and 7/8 held-out gate classifications. These are not scientific answer-accuracy measurements.

Design Choices and Creativity
Ranking scores are not probabilities. Unknown conditions are never labeled safe. Public access alone is not treated as permission to index a report. When no evidence matches a search, the app shows an empty state instead of an invented conclusion.

Impact and Next Steps
CombustionLens makes the boundaries of microgravity fire-safety evidence auditable for Moon and Mars mission planning. Next steps are independent review of run-level records, broader evaluation and a validated public deployment. No NASA endorsement is claimed.
